chord.reason: a stl file carries triangles and nothing else. The surface they stand for is not in it, so how far they sit from it cannot be measured from this input by any means. What the mesher will see IS these triangles.

centrelines.why: the section enclosing the mouth's centre is 0.20 of the mouth's own passage area, so the centre is not inside its own passage (an annulus, or a mouth whose face is not across the passage)

local_feature_size.why: A local feature size from the medial axis is not given. The medial axis of a triangulated surface is not the medial axis of the solid it stands for at any tessellation density: every convex edge adds a spurious branch, and the filters that prune them have no setting that is right across parts. A size read off it would be a property of the tessellator, reported as a property of the part.
evidence: docs/research_computational_geometry.md 1.2: continuity of the medial axis needs C2 closeness (Chazal and Soufflet via Attali et al.), which no tessellation has

docs/research_computational_geometry.md 3.1 and 3.2, MEASURED on this corpus: an unfiltered shrinking-ball medial size read 0.00005 where the smallest passage is 0.0399 (800x too small), and no separation angle was right on more than 3 of 6 parts
docs/synthesis.md 2.1: do not emit a single filtered medial minimum
what IS given instead: the passage's own section, area and hydraulic diameter, at every station of every centreline (`centrelines[].stations`), which is a plane section and converges

vertex_curvature.why: A per-vertex curvature is not given. Discrete mean curvature provably does not converge on a tessellated cylinder: with every vertex exactly on the surface it oscillates between about -3 and 0 as the mesh refines, from the valence pattern alone, and a CAD export's long thin facets are the condition under which the cheap operators fail worst.
evidence: docs/research_computational_geometry.md 4.2: Gatzke and Grimm, sensitivity to tangential vertex motion

what IS given instead: a radius fitted over each whole crease patch that is a cylinder or a sphere, with its residual, and refused when the residual is large (`partition.patches[].radius`), and the bend radius of each centreline turn (`centrelines[].bends[].radius`)

fluid_side.why: a ring with one hole through a thick body is the end of an annular passage (the file is the fluid) or the mouth of a bore through a solid (the file is the metal), and the two are the same shape
